$comment: STT render-kernel time-filter contract (renderer-abstraction-2026-06 §5.1). The scalar time-filter alpha has ONE definition — @poopdeck.gl/core/time-filter's timeFilterAlpha — and a second, independently-derived branchless statement of the same four formulas as an Expr AST in @poopdeck.gl/core/shader-codegen (ALPHA_EXPR + evalExpr). Every renderer backend HAND-WRITES its own shader in its own dialect; none is machine-emitted. What prevents drift is the per-backend conformance obligation in `conformance` below, not codegen. This file STATES the frozen op-set and those obligations so both are declared contracts, not facts discovered by reading source. Enforced by packages/core/test/render-spec-contract.test.ts.

opSemantics.step: step(edge, x) = x >= edge ? 1 : 0 (GLSL step argument order)
opSemantics.select: select(c, t, f) = c != 0 ? t : f; emitted as a ternary and evaluated lazily, so an untaken div-by-zero branch is never computed

second.form: branchless step/select composition over the frozen op-set
second.$comment: Independently derived on purpose: two derivations disagree where the SPEC is ambiguous, which one implementation can never reveal. Pinned equal to `primary` by a 2000-sample randomized sweep in packages/core/test/shader-codegen.test.ts.

conformance.$comment: Every backend hand-writes its shader. Each MUST carry a conformance test that pins its shader math to BOTH oracles — so editing a formula in one dialect goes red until every renderer follows. Enforced structurally: render-spec-contract.test.ts asserts each backend package's test suite references both oracle modules. Shader source cannot execute headless, so the last leg is a structural lock (verbatim formula-line assertions) rather than execution; packages/maplibre/test/time-modes.test.ts is the reference implementation of the whole pattern.
obligations: backend JS reference == primary oracle, over a dense sweep including boundary and degenerate inputs
shipped shader source == backend JS reference, by structural lock
genuine divergences are pinned explicitly with an explaining comment, never hidden by a loosened tolerance or a skipped case

backends.$comment: Mode dispatch is by UNIFORM VALUE at draw time (cumulative > wake > trail > window), not per-mode shader variants — the extension is a singleton whose memoized getShaders() exists to avoid a pipeline re-link per tile.
Mode is chosen at shader-BUILD time (buildPointVertexSource picks the snippet), so each mode ships as an independent function.

Also carries a three-local hard 0|1 vertex-collapse mirror (tsl/time-filter-math.ts's *Visible) with the safe-collapse invariant `visible === 0 implies alpha === 0`; that invariant is part of this backend's obligation.
Cesium's shipped path calls the primary oracle per feature per frame on the CPU; it has no GPU time-filter shader. Its obligation is to keep calling the oracle rather than drift to a local copy.

$emittersComment: Empty on purpose, and it is a decision rather than an omission. `emitGLSL100` was deleted first (no callers, byte-identical output to the 3.00 emitter), then `emitGLSL300` and its sole caller @poopdeck.gl/cesium's `timeFilterAlphaGlsl` were removed at the 0.6.0 cut for the same reason: no shipped shader was ever generated from the AST, and every backend hand-writes its shader in its own dialect. The AST (`ALPHA_EXPR`) and its CPU evaluator (`evalExpr`) survive and are load-bearing — they are the SECOND ORACLE each backend's shader math is pinned to. Re-add an emitter only alongside something that compiles its output.

exclusions.$comment: Deliberately OUTSIDE the frozen op-set; each stays per-backend, pinned to the CPU oracle by parity tests rather than codegen.
exclusions.wakeSizeScale: vertex-stage size multiplier (not a fragment alpha)
